requirements.title: Social and ethical responsibilities of computing
requirements.summary: Satisfy at least one program requirement or elective using a listed SERC-qualified subject; this is an overlay, not necessarily an additional course.

requirements.title: Additional Course 6 or 18 elective
requirements.summary: The unversioned chart permits one subject satisfying a Course 6 or Course 18 degree requirement, with a 12–15-unit slot. This is a published eligibility criterion. The department’s 6-4_2025 version separately specifies named EECS/graduate pools and an open MATH criterion; the two source scopes are not silently equated.

requirements.title: Second CI-M subject
requirements.summary: The unversioned chart requires a second CI-M subject beyond the application choice. A named CIM2 pool has now been verified for the department’s explicit 6-4_2025 version; applicability differences between that version and the catalog chart remain unresolved.

requirements.title: SERC module credit condition
requirements.summary: Credit for 6.C01 requires completion of a 6-unit disciplinary module; consult an advisor. Do not treat its listed 6 units as sufficient by itself.

requirements.title: General Institute Requirements
requirements.summary: The chart summarizes 17 GIR subjects: six science, eight HASS (at least two CI-H), two REST (identified as 6.1200 and 18.C06), and one laboratory requirement (identified as 6.1010, 12 units). Detailed distributions and choice pools remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Physical education and swimming
requirements.summary: The Course 6-4 chart summarizes swimming plus four physical-education courses for eight points. The institute GIR source separately provides the transfer-entry reduction and other completion paths; see its linked policy note.

requirements.title: Major, GIR overlap and degree accounting
requirements.summary: The chart reports 168–177 major units, 36 major units also satisfying GIRs, and 180–189 units beyond the GIRs. Units for any of the 17 GIR subjects cannot also count toward units required beyond the GIRs. Ranges are preserved, not replaced with a fabricated single total.

requirements.title: Linked general CI-M reference list
requirements.summary: The degree chart links this general EECS CI-M list, but the page does not identify a CIM2 subset. These course observations are a reference pool, not a verified set of second-CI-M choices for Course 6-4.

requirements.title: Minimum attendance and approved program
requirements.summary: Attend at least three regular academic terms, ordinarily including the graduation term, and complete an approved GIR and departmental program. Departmental deviations need department permission; GIR substitutions require the appropriate faculty-committee petition.

requirements.title: Transfer cohort requirements
requirements.summary: Transfer students normally follow requirements for the class they join on entry; the source does not assign an entry year to this program record.

requirements.title: Units beyond GIRs
requirements.summary: At least 48 unrestricted elective units belong within the program-specific units beyond GIRs. ROTC units are excluded. CI-M units generally count beyond GIRs, except when that subject also supplies one of the 17 GIR subjects. Use the Course 6-4 chart for its specific unit range.

requirements.title: Calculus advanced credit
requirements.summary: Existing AP, advanced-standing or transfer credit for 18.01 is lost on taking 18.01; taking 18.01A instead earns three elective units. Placement and subject-specific calculus policies require the linked mathematics guidance.

requirements.title: Physics sequencing and advanced credit
requirements.summary: A Physics I GIR credit must precede enrollment in a Physics II GIR subject, even when mixing sequences. Students with AP or advanced-standing 8.01 credit who take 8.012 receive six elective units in place of 8.01.

requirements.title: Communication totals and annual pace
requirements.summary: Complete two CI-H/HW and two major-specific CI-M subjects. Minimum cumulative progress is one by year one, two by year two, three by year three and four by graduation. Only one CI-H per term counts, while multiple CI-M or a concurrent CI-H and CI-M may count. Noncompliance is referred to academic-performance review.

requirements.title: First communication subject placement
requirements.summary: The first CI subject must be CI-HW unless the First-year Essay Evaluation permits CI-H/CI-HW, AP English Language or Literature is 5, or higher-level IB English A/B is 7. An eligible student may still choose CI-HW. Pass the first CI-H/HW by the end of the second term.

requirements.title: Communication for double majors
requirements.summary: Double majors must meet the CI-M component of each major plus two CI-H subjects. Four CI-M subjects are normal; a subject common to both departments may satisfy both when permitted.

requirements.title: HASS minimum and distribution criteria
requirements.summary: Complete eight HASS-designated subjects, including one from each distribution category: humanities, arts and social sciences. Two CI-H/HW subjects may simultaneously meet communication requirements. Eligibility is defined by official designation; this rule does not invent a fixed course list.

requirements.title: HASS concentration and deadlines
requirements.summary: Complete a field-specific three- or four-subject HASS concentration with its designated advisor. Submit the proposal by the end of the first week of the second junior-year term and completion form by the end of the first week of the final graduation term. One distribution subject may overlap with advisor permission. A special concentration needs advance approval; field-specific rules remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Remaining HASS eligibility
requirements.summary: After distribution and concentration, remaining slots in the eight-subject total may use subjects in any HASS distribution category or designated HASS electives.

requirements.title: REST selection and departmental restriction
requirements.summary: Complete two REST-designated subjects, ordinarily no more than one from the student’s department; jointly offered J subjects are exempt from that departmental limit. Departmental degree subjects may simultaneously satisfy REST. Course 6-4 identifies 6.1200[J] and 18.C06[J] as its normal route; substitutions require review.

requirements.title: Laboratory-designated credit
requirements.summary: Complete 12 units specifically designated as Institute Laboratory credit; subjects may be combined, and designated laboratory credit can differ from total subject units. Subject units above the 12 needed count beyond GIRs. Course 6-4 identifies 6.1010 as its normal route.

requirements.title: PE, transfer and swimming paths
requirements.summary: First-year entrants complete four PE/wellness courses for eight points; transfer entrants complete two courses for four points. Both must satisfy swimming through a beginning swim class or test. Each varsity year earns four points; each ROTC year earns two, capped at four. Approved training/swim/exercise options may earn points. Finish by the end of year two or submit an extension plan. PE points are not academic units.

requirements.title: Undergraduate academic-performance review
requirements.summary: The CAP normally accepts at least 36 units per regular term with a term rating above 3.0/5, unless it has imposed a higher individual standard. Falling below this triggers individual review rather than an automatic graduation GPA cutoff. The cumulative 3.0 federal-aid criterion is a separate financial-aid rule.

requirements.title: Passing and nonpassing grades
requirements.summary: D is generally passing, but a department may require additional work or repetition before the next subject. Authorized P corresponds to A–C performance; first-year DN/FN do not earn credit. Exact first-year and flexible P/NR eligibility remains subject to separate policy review.

requirements.title: Incomplete grades at graduation
requirements.summary: Resolve ordinary I grades before graduation, and no ordinary I can be assigned in the graduation term. The exceptional emergency IE notation carries no credit but need not be resolved before graduation; the source distinguishes these cases.

requirements.title: Degree application and clearance
requirements.summary: Submit the SB degree application by the relevant academic-calendar deadline. Award requires faculty approval following committee/department recommendation, cleared financial obligations and no pending disciplinary actions.

requirements.title: Department declaration availability
requirements.summary: The department says students could declare Course 6-4 beginning Fall 2022. This is declaration evidence, not proof of the first instructional offering or of the applicable curriculum version.

requirements.title: Departmental substitutions and petitions
requirements.summary: Discuss a proposed substitution with the advisor, then submit a departmental petition for advisor comments and department action. Decisions are individual, never automatically guaranteed by another student’s approval. Submit early, including before taking a proposed substitute, rather than waiting until the final semester. The student-specific audit is restricted to current EECS students and is not part of this public-source inventory.

requirements.title: Version 6-4_2025 applicability
requirements.summary: The public department source labels this version 6-4_2025, requires it for students entering MIT in Fall 2025 or later, and says subject lists are current as of Fall 2026. Those labels are curriculum applicability evidence, not a first-offered date or an inferred catalog edition.

requirements.title: Version 6-4_2025: CIM2 overlay
requirements.summary: For this stated version, at least two completed subjects must belong to the listed CIM2 pool. This is an additional constraint across the program, not two extra required subject slots. It differs from the unversioned catalog reference inventory; version reconciliation remains explicit.

requirements.title: Version 6-4_2025: subject reuse
requirements.summary: Each completed subject may fill at most one required subject slot but may satisfy multiple additional constraints, including center, SERC and CIM2 designations. Do not impose separate unique subjects for every overlay.

requirements.title: Version 6-4_2025: open mathematics elective criterion
requirements.summary: The MATH option permits any non-calculus subject satisfying a Course 18 SB requirement, provided its content is not essentially similar to other subjects counted toward this degree. This is an eligibility criterion, not a fabricated finite list.

notes: Partial degree inventory. The unversioned catalog chart and explicit department version 6-4_2025 are separate evidence contexts. The latter applies to Fall 2025+ entrants and identifies its subject lists as of Fall 2026. No catalog edition or program launch date is inferred from version labels, retrieval date or the request cache-buster.

The public requirements endpoint is embedded by the official EECS Course 6-4 page. Its plugin timestamp is a request cache-buster, not source publication metadata. No student-specific audit or authenticated resource was accessed.

The department version adds choices absent from the unversioned chart, including 6.3930, some joint/module alternatives and graduate elective pools. This batch maps its CIM2 pool, reuse constraint and open MATH criterion but does not silently replace or combine the entire chart inventory. Full version reconciliation remains a requirement gap.

The chart gives 6.4300 as 15 units; its linked general CI-M list gives 12. The versioned department annotation shows 4-0-11, but no unit-definition or source-precedence decision is inferred. Curated credits remain null pending explicit reconciliation.

Science GIR choices are mapped from six official sections. Their catalog table lists codes and units without titles; names remain unknown. HASS designation, distribution, concentration and advisor-approval criteria are rules, not a fabricated finite course list. Field-specific HASS concentration requirements remain unreviewed.

REST and laboratory normal routes are named by the Course 6-4 chart. Institute criteria, departmental restriction, joint-subject exception and laboratory-designated unit accounting are recorded. Optional substitute-pool membership is not asserted exhaustively.

Institute rules now include three-term attendance, petitions, communication pace/placement, HASS deadlines, transfer PE reduction, degree application and clearance. CAP academic-standing review is distinguished from the financial-aid GPA criterion and from a graduation GPA minimum.
The department explicitly permits declaring Course 6-4 starting Fall 2022. This is declaration availability, not verified first instruction; first_offered stays null.

The versioned CIM2 parser observes subject annotations and prerequisites. Existing unversioned course metadata is not overwritten across versions; fresh source-specific observations remain separately reviewable. Individual descriptions, most prerequisites, public course sites and syllabi remain unknown. Credit unit ranges are not collapsed.
